articles.title: Ilia Topuria: "Si me dice que me voy a quedar ciego, que le den a Justin y a todo el mundo"
articles.standfirst: 'El Matador' se sinceró acerca de las lesiones que sufrió en la Casa Blanca ante Gaethje y cómo lo vivió desde dentro
articles.summary: 'El Matador' se sinceró acerca de las lesiones que sufrió en la Casa Blanca ante Gaethje y cómo lo vivió desde dentro
articles.body: El pasado 14 de junio, Ilia Topuria vivió la noche más oscura de su carrera en las MMA tras ser finalizado por Justin Gaethje y perder el invicto y el cinturón de peso ligero. Su hermano Aleksandre decidió parar el combate antes de que diese inicio el quinto asalto, al ver cómo su hermano mayor tenía fracturados los dos orbitales, la nariz y el pie, e Ilia ha hablado al respecto de ese suceso y de cómo lo vivió desde dentro. Antes de que diese comienzo el cuarto asalto, el árbitro Marc Goddard y el doctor ya le dijeron a Ilia que iban a parar el combate al ver cómo tenía el rostro. Sin embargo, 'El Matador' insistió en que estaba bien y logró convencerles por el contexto de la situación. Campeón invicto, en la Casa Blanca, en la cartelera más importante de la historia... No podía acabar así. "Cuando entra el doctor, me dice que me va a parar la pelea y yo le dije que no, que me secara el ojo, que me quitara la sangre, que hiciera algo para que siguiera porque físicamente estaba bien, yo no quería parar. Es una pelea que marca una vida, o varias, no solo la mía y la de Justin", ha revelado en una entrevista con 'ABC'. Sin embargo, cuando su hermano Aleksandre se dió cuenta de la gravedad de la situación y de que era imposible que Ilia diese la vuelta a la pelea en el quinto, decidió que ya era suficiente. Una decisión que salvó la carrera de Topuria, ya que a posteriori se supo que si hubiese seguido recibiendo golpes podría haberse quedado ciego. Demoledor. De hecho, Topuria ha agradecido a su hermano esta decisión de parar la pelea por el hecho de que él nunca hubiese dado el paso. Un peleador no piensa en rendirse cuando está en el octágono, y menos Ilia. Eso sí, si hubiese sabido lo peligroso que era seguir combatiendo ha dejado claro que no habría dudado en rendirse, tal y como ha confirmado una vez ha sabido el riesgo que tomó. "Con que me dijera que no me iba a quedar ciego me valía para seguir. Porque si me dice que me voy a quedar ciego, que le den a Justin y a todo el mundo, porque no quiero nada en mi vida si me voy a quedar ciego", finalizó. Ilia define su lesión en los orbitales como si le hubiesen tirado cristales, ya que le ardían ambos ojos y se le pegaban los párpados por la sangre. Incluso en el segundo asalto ha revelado que no podía ver bien, de ahí que se lanzase a por Gaethje al suelo una vez le dañó con un golpe al hígado. Casi cinco meses después de aquel día, Topuria es consciente de que su carrera pudo haberse acabado, pero ha recibido una segunda oportunidad para redimirse de aquello y demostrar que sigue destinado a convertirse en uno de los mejores de todos los tiempos.

articles.title: 'Please take the job!' - Trump asks UFC boss Dana White to be White House press secretary
articles.summary: The BBC has asked the White House and UFC whether the president's job offer is genuine.
articles.body:
US President Donald Trump has asked Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) boss Dana White to be White House press secretary, in a social media post.

"Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other," Trump wrote on Truth Social. "Dana, please take the job!"

It's unclear whether the president's public job offer is genuine. The BBC has asked the White House and UFC, along with its parent company TKO Group Holdings, for comment.

The vacancy for White House press secretary has been open since mid-October, when Katie Zacharia exited after just a few days on the job.

Trump's post comes after his fellow Republicans were routed in the US midterm elections, losing their congressional majorities.

In Saturday afternoon's post, Trump called White "a violent Fighter and Warrior" and asked that he bring a number of high-profile UFC fighters with him on the job "even though some are not from our Country".

"We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left," Trump wrote, alongside photos of the six fighters.

Following Trump's post, White posted an Instagram photo of himself behind the lectern in the White House press briefing room.

"On to the next chapter," White's post said, though it was unclear if the post was tongue-in-cheek.

White, who is also the chief of Zuffa Boxing, was ringside for a fight in London on Saturday between British former world champion Chris Billam-Smith and Jamaican-born Briton Cheavon Clarke at the Copper Box Arena.

The BBC was trying to reach him for comment.

Famously combative, White has at times clashed with journalists covering the sport during news conferences.

In 2020, he released a video targeting reporters who had questioned the UFC's decision to hold fights early in the pandemic.

In 2009, he released an expletive-laden video tirade using an anti-gay slur while rebutting a journalist's story about changes to backstage credentialing rules at UFC events.

White is a longtime ally - and friend - of Trump.

When White and his business partners bought the then-struggling UFC organisation for $2m in 2001, the sport was facing intense bipartisan backlash.

Just five years earlier, Republican Senator John McCain had famously labelled mixed martial arts "human cockfighting", sparking bans in 36 US states.

"None of the venues wanted [the UFC]," White told CBS, the BBC's US partner, in 2025. "They didn't believe in it. They didn't like it, and they were worried about the type of crowd that would show up for this type of event."

With mainstream arenas shutting them out, White credits Trump with saving the organisation by hosting two UFC events at the Trump Taj Mahal casino in Atlantic City, New Jersey, in 2001.

This summer, the UFC held a cage match on the White House lawn.

White became a speaker for Trump's White House campaigns at the Republican National Conventions in 2016, 2020 and 2024.

articles.title: Donald Trump ofrece a Dana White, presidente de la UFC, ser el nuevo secretario de prensa de la Casa Blanca
articles.standfirst: Ambos guardan una gran relación desde hace años
articles.summary: Ambos guardan una gran relación desde hace años
articles.body: Ver para creer. Según ha comunicado el propio Donald Trump, el presidente estadounidense ha pedido al presidente de la UFC, Dana White, que sea el nuevo secretario de prensa de la Casa Blanca. Ambos, cabe recordar, guardan una gran relación desde hace años, se les ha visto hacer campaña (a favor de Trump) juntos e incluso Dana White 'entregó' a Trump el pasado UFC Casa Blanca de junio (en el que Topuria perdió ante Gaethje) como regalo de cumpleaños al mandatario. "Dana será un secretario de prensa como ningún otro", escribió Trump en su plataforma 'Truth Social'. "¡Dana, por favor, acepta el puesto!", ampliaba. Este aún no se ha pronunciado. Pero no acaba ahí. Trump ha pedido a Dana White, definido por el presidente de los Estados Unidos como "un violento luchador y guerrero", que incorpore a su equipo a varios peleadores o ex peleadores de la UFC. "He solicitado que traiga consigo a un equipo de colaboradores, algunos de los cuales no son de nuestro país, entre ellos Islam Makhachev, Khabib Nurmagomedov, Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier, Amanda Nunes y Kayla Harrison", escribía Trump.

articles.title: Trump Says He's Asked UFC's Dana White to Be His Press Secretary. No One Will Say If He's Joking
articles.summary: WEST PALM BEACH, Fla. (AP) — President Donald Trump said Saturday that he has offered the job of White House press secretary to his friend and UFC boss Dana White, an announcement unconventional even for the norm-busting president and one that nobody in the White House immediately confirmed.
articles.body:
WEST PALM BEACH, Fla. (AP) — President Donald Trump said Saturday that he has offered the job of White House press secretary to his friend and UFC boss Dana White, an announcement unconventional even for the norm-busting president and one that nobody in the White House immediately confirmed.

Trump, while he was at his golf club in Florida, posted on social media that he made the offer to "the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior" to become the Republican president's chief spokesperson.

Trump said he requested that White bring along several UFC fighters as "assistants," adding, "We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left. Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other. Dana, please take the job!"

The White House did not respond Saturday to messages inquiring about the Truth Social post.

White was in London on Saturday for a boxing event. A spokesperson for UFC did not immediately respond to messages seeking comment.

The UFC head shared an image of Trump's post on Instagram, along with an image of himself standing behind the podium in the White House press briefing room with the words "On to the next chapter."

Trump's post came as his White House is in a period of major transition and struggling with his party's deep losses in Tuesday's midterm elections. The historic wins by Democratic candidates, including in areas that Republicans had held for decades, led to the GOP losing control of both chambers of Congress.

Trump on Friday announced he was replacing his longtime adviser Susie Wiles, who was seen as something of a tempering force on the president's impulses, with aide Stephen Miller to serve as the next chief of staff. Miller is known as the architect of the administration's hard-line immigration policies and is among the most determined of Trump's inner circle.

The shake-up at the heart of his administration follows the brief but tumultuous week when Trump tried out a new press secretary in Katie Zacharia, who seemed uncomfortable in her sole appearance before reporters before leaving the job after five days.

The post had been vacant since Karoline Leavitt left at the end of August. Trump remains without a chief spokesperson.

Trump is close friends with White and has attended several UFC events with him since returning to the White House in January 2025.

He brought White and the sport to the White House's South Lawn in June for the celebration of America's 250th year of its independence and the president's own 80th birthday. A wire-mesh Octagon was constructed near the executive mansion under " The Claw," a spaceship-like metal arch fitted with lights, sound equipment and large screens.

"It was an amazing experience, this was a one-of-one," said White afterward.

White also spoke at the Republican National Conventions in 2016, 2020 and 2024.

articles.title: Donald Trump offers White House press secretary job to UFC CEO Dana White
articles.summary: Trump announced his offer to White on his Truth Social platform, referring to the UFC chief as "a violent warrior."
articles.body:
U.S. President Donald Trump offered the open White House press secretary position to UFC chief executive Dana White in a social media post on Saturday.

"I am pleased to announce that the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior, has been offered the job of Press Secretary of the United States," Trump wrote in a post on his Truth Social platform. "I have requested that he bring with him assistants, even though some are not from our Country, of Islam Makhachev, Khabib Nurmagomedov, Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier, Amanda Nunes, and Kayla Harris," Trump added. "We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left. Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other. Dana, please take the job! President DONALD J. TRUMP"

"I am pleased to announce that the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior, has been offered the job of Press Secretary of the United States," Trump wrote in a post on his Truth Social platform.

"I have requested that he bring with him assistants, even though some are not from our Country, of Islam Makhachev, Khabib Nurmagomedov, Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier, Amanda Nunes, and Kayla Harris," Trump added. "We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left. Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other. Dana, please take the job! President DONALD J. TRUMP"

Trump name-dropped several UFC fighters that White could presumably bring with him to the White House podium to interact with reporters. However, he mistyped the name of Kayla Harrison, arguably the top women's fighter in the world . A two-time Olympic gold medalist and UFC bantamweight champion, Harrison will defend her title at next week's UFC 334 event at New York's Madison Square Garden.

The White House has not officially responded to Trump's post, creating some uncertainty as to whether or not this was a serious invitation, according to the Associated Pres s .

White, in London for Saturday's Zuffa Boxing 12 event , also has not directly responded to the president's announcement. However, he posted a screen shot of Trump's announcement on an Instagram story, along with an image of himself at the podium of the White House press briefing room with the caption, "On to the next chapter."

Trump and White have known each other for at least 25 years

The relationship between the U.S. president and White dates back to 2001, when Trump's Taj Mahal hotel and casino in Atlantic City, New Jersey hosted a UFC event. At the time, New Jersey was one of the few states that sanctioned UFC cards, which were banned in 36 states.

Since then, the two have developed a friendship as Trump has attended several UFC events over the past 25 years — including four as sitting U.S. president. White introduced Trump at the 2024 Republican National Convention, in addition to speaking at the 2016 and 2020 events.

The most public display of the Trump-White partnership was the UFC Freedom 250 event that was held on the South Lawn of the White House in June. The main event of that card was an upset win by UFC lightweight champion Justin Gaethje , whose name was referenced in Trump's Truth Social post.

UFC holding an event at the White House raised White's already high profile , resulting in interviews with NPR, Rolling Stone and the New Yorker, and an appearance on the cover of Time magazine. White defended Trump in those interviews and implied that he had an advisory role during the 2024 presidential campaign.

The press secretary position became open just over two weeks ago when Katie Zacharia resigned after only five days on the job . Previously a conservative commentator and advisor for the company that runs Truth Social, Zacharia received immediate scrutiny after an initial press briefing that lasted only five minutes, followed by questions over whether she was actually a lawyer , as claimed.

Zacharia took over for Karoline Leavitt, who left the press secretary role in August following the birth of her second child. During Leavitt's maternity leave, other officials in the Trump administration held press briefings, including Vice President JD Vance, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.

articles.body: Uncrowned has Chris Billam-Smith vs. Chev Clarke live results, round-by-round updates, ring walks and start time for the Zuffa Boxing 12 fight card on Saturday at the Copper Box Arena in London, England. In the night's main event, former WBO cruiserweight champion Chris Billam-Smith faces Chev Clarke in a 10-round cruiserweight clash.Billam-Smith (22-2, 14 KOs) returns to the ring following a seventh-round stoppage victory over Ryan Rozicki in June. The Brit held the WBO cruiserweight world title from 2023-2024 before losing a unanimous decision to Gilberto "Zurdo" Ramirez in a unification bout.Clarke (12-2, 9 KOs) enters Saturday's contest following a dramatic seventh-round stoppage victory over Jack Massey in June. The 2024 Olympian recovered from two fourth-round knockdowns to defeat Massey.Clarke defeated Billam-Smith twice in the unpaid ranks, including the final of the 2016 English national championships.In the night's co-main event, former WBO middleweight champion Denzel Bentley (22-3-1, 18 KOs) takes on Shane Mosley Jr. (23-5, 15 KOs) in a 10-round contest.
